key_highlights: ASX rises on Wall Street's best day in six weeks; big four banks lead gains as oil prices and bond yields ease
RBA chief flags inflation concerns; IMF urges spending cuts ahead of a likely further rate hike
Recession odds for 2027 rising per macrobusiness; petrol price shock and fuel supply crunch at east-coast ports add pressure
Iron ore sentiment weak ('roaches seethe'); LNG export imbalance with Japan as east coast starves
Anthropic secures $31bn datacentre deal in western Queensland; AI regulation and foreign interference concerns mount
Qantas ground staff strike threat over 'Joyce-era' bargaining; school-holiday travel disruption risk
Housing hits 'absurdly unaffordable' levels; ACCC moves to break real estate agency monopoly; tenants see rent relief
WA exploration pipeline active: Dalaroo copper-nickel-PGE, Critica rare earths, Augustus gold targets

sectors.trend: Iron ore sentiment weak; WA exploration active across copper-nickel-PGE, rare earths, and gold. Commodity price softness pressures BHP/RIO/FMG near-term.
sectors.implications: Short-term headwind for iron ore majors; selective upside in WA junior explorers (Critica, Augustus) on positive drill results.

sectors.trend: Big four banks advance on easing yields; however, soaring state interest costs and IMF spending-cut pressure create fiscal headwinds. RBA inflation worry supports higher-for-longer rates.
sectors.implications: NIMs supported by elevated rates but credit-risk and sovereign-debt concerns cap multiples. CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX constructive short-term.

sectors.trend: Crude retreats as Middle East supply fears ease; domestic fuel supply crunch at east-coast ports; petrol price shock; Victoria backs away from renewable transmission; coal policy debate intensifies.
sectors.implications: Woodside (WDS.AX) and Santos (STO.AX) face LNG export imbalance risk; coal names (BHP.AX coal segment) benefit from policy uncertainty. Fuel distributors under margin pressure.

sectors.trend: Coles holds milk prices despite axing farmer support; Qantas strike threat disrupts travel; Cue and Veronika Maine face collapse. Petrol shock hits household budgets.
sectors.implications: WES.AX and WES.AX face margin and reputational risk; QAN.AX exposed to strike disruption. Consumer staples defensive but pricing power under scrutiny.

sectors.trend: Anthropic $31bn QLD datacentre deal signals major capex inflow; AI regulation proposals (rogue-incident reporting) and foreign-interference warnings add policy risk.
sectors.implications: Long-term positive for Australian data/infrastructure plays; short-term regulatory uncertainty. Limited direct ASX exposure but supportive for telcos (TPG.AX, VHC.AX).

sectors.trend: Housing 'absurdly unaffordable'; tenants see rent relief; ACCC targets real estate agency monopoly. Mixed signals for residential REITs.
sectors.implications: Residential REITs (e.g., GPT.AX, ICPS.AX) face rent-ceiling pressure but occupancy support. Commercial REITs (MER.AX, SPG.AX) benefit from rate easing.

key_themes: RBA inflation persistence vs. IMF fiscal-tightening call
Commodity softness (iron ore, oil) vs. WA exploration upside
Fuel supply crunch and petrol price shock as inflationary risk
AI infrastructure build-out (Anthropic QLD) vs. regulatory tightening
Housing affordability crisis and ACCC intervention
Qantas industrial action as consumer-disruption risk
State government interest-cost burden constraining fiscal space

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA further rate hike / inflation re-acceleration
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight financials (NIM benefit); underweight rate-sensitive REITs and growth equities; monitor CPI print.
Maintain defensive allocation to staples, healthcare, utilities; reduce cyclical mining exposure.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Fuel supply crunch / petrol price shock
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor Woodside/Santos LNG logistics; consider fuel-distributor short exposure; watch RBA response.
Avoid QAN.AX ahead of strike; monitor tourism-linked REITs and consumer discretionary.
Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX weight; rotate into WA junior explorers with optionality.
Monitor residential REIT rent yields; ACCC action may compress agency margins but support tenant demand.

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight big four banks on rate-supportive NIMs and easing yields
opportunities.rationale: Banks advance as bond yields ease; RBA higher-for-longer supports spreads; IMF fiscal tightening limits credit risk.

opportunities.recommendation: Selective exposure to WA exploration names on positive drill/survey results
opportunities.rationale: Dalaroo copper-nickel-PGE, Critica rare earths, Augustus gold targets offer asymmetric upside vs. weak iron ore.

opportunities.recommendation: Long-term positioning in AI infrastructure / datacentre beneficiaries
opportunities.rationale: Anthropic $31bn QLD deal signals sustained capex; telco and data-centre REITs benefit from structural demand.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore and oil-exposed mining weight
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore sentiment weak; crude retreating; Middle East supply fears easing removes upside catalyst.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid Qantas and travel-linked names ahead of strike
defensive_moves.rationale: Ground staff strike over Joyce-era agreements; school-holiday disruption risk to revenue and sentiment.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain defensive tilt: healthcare, utilities, consumer staples
defensive_moves.rationale: Rising 2027 recession odds and petrol shock favour defensive sectors; housing unaffordability caps cyclicals.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to consolidate near recent highs on bank strength and easing yields, but Qantas strike, fuel crunch, and RBA inflation commentary cap upside. Volatility elevated ahead of Fed decision and RBA signals.
market_outlook.long_term: Rising 2027 recession odds, IMF fiscal-tightening call, and housing unaffordability create a cautious 6–12 month backdrop. Structural AI capex (Anthropic QLD) and WA exploration provide selective pockets of growth. Rate path remains the dominant variable.
